clue.text: Uncovered one announcing his discovery

parts.note: surface reading: someone unveiling or revealing a new finding to the world
setter's reading: literally naked, like the Greek mathematician who leapt from his bath and ran through Syracuse shouting Eureka

explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' looks like it means revealed, but it means unclothed: the legend has the mathematician running naked from the bath crying 'Eureka!'
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek scientist famously discovered the principle of displacement in his bath and ran naked through the streets proclaiming it.

clue.text: Help to support traveller, like victim of divine vengeance

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it is written after the other

parts.note: a rep is a commercial traveller, a sales representative
aid is help

explanation.surface: Assistance is offered to a wanderer who has been struck down by the gods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord' (Romans) makes someone so punished paid back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone punished by heaven has been paid back for their misdeeds, in the biblical sense of vengeance as repayment.

clue.text: Instrument in band, oddly, in the pit

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it, so the shuffled letters go within the next piece

parts.note: the pit is hell, the bottomless pit

indicators.note: arranged oddly means put in a strange order, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A musician in a group plays strangely down in the orchestra pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like a call for odd letters, but here it shuffles all four letters of band.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbell is a small bell held and swung by hand, often played in tuned sets, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Substance, and a bit of brass, to reach the peak

parts.note: matter is substance
a horn is one instrument of a brass section

explanation.surface: Physical material and a brass instrument are needed to climb to the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit of brass' tempts toward a first letter; it is a whole instrument from the brass family.
explanation.definitionFit: The Matterhorn is the famous pyramid-shaped Alpine mountain on the Swiss-Italian border, the peak above all others.

clue.text: Weight-lifter demonstrates the German strain

parts.note: der is the German for the
to rick is to sprain or wrench, as a back

explanation.surface: A German weightlifter shows what happens when you pull a muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weight-lifter' suggests an athlete, but it is a machine for hoisting loads.
explanation.definitionFit: A derrick is a crane with a pivoting arm used for hoisting heavy loads, as on docks or over oil wells.

clue.text: Say the main areas or positions of church authority

indicators.note: say means speak aloud, so the next phrase stands for a word of the same sound

parts.note: the main is the open sea, so its areas are seas

explanation.surface: A churchman lists the ocean regions alongside ecclesiastical positions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old poetic word for the sea, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is his diocese or the throne from which he governs it, so sees are seats of church authority.

clue.text: Otter has ruined the current-control device

indicators.note: something ruined is broken apart, so these letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An otter has damaged the device that controls the flow of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' with an otter about suggests a stream; it is electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to regulate electric current, as in a light dimmer.

clue.text: Marshal imprisons 200, including classical type, for witchcraft

indicators.note: a prisoner is held inside, so the marshal's name surrounds what follows

parts.note: Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the number holds the next piece within it

parts.note: CC is 200 in Roman numerals
roman is the upright style of type, as opposed to italic

explanation.surface: A military officer locks up two hundred people, among them an ancient Roman, on charges of sorcery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' looks like an anagram signal but is Napoleon's marshal Ney.
explanation.definitionFit: Necromancy, strictly divination by summoning the dead, is used generally for black magic or sorcery.

clue.text: Outwit in a game of cards

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to get the better of someone by trickery
second meaning: a trick-taking card game popular in North America

explanation.surface: Someone gets the better of their opponents during a hand of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game's name became a verb for outmanoeuvring a player, and from that, for outsmarting anyone at all.

clue.text: Old textile worker liable to be missed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: historically, a woman whose trade was spinning yarn

definitions.note: a phrase describing a person, standing for the noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: an unmarried woman, the sort addressed as Miss

explanation.surface: A craftswoman from a vanished trade who might be fondly remembered once gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missed' looks like regret at absence, but here it means called Miss, the title for an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The word began as the name for a woman who spun thread and later came to mean an unmarried woman, one properly titled Miss.

clue.text: When streets are crowded in time for the first film-show?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the busy commuting period morning and evening
second meaning, whimsical: rushes are the first prints of a day's filming, so this would be the hour for viewing them

explanation.surface: Someone hurries through packed streets to catch the opening screening at a cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: In film-making, 'rushes' are the unedited first prints shown to the director after a day's shooting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally names the peak commuting period, and jokingly the hour set aside for screening a film's rushes.

clue.text: 'ow to protect one's bet with advantage

indicators.note: the dropped aitch of a Cockney 'how' tells us to drop the opening H from the word that follows

parts.note: to hedge is to protect yourself against losing a bet

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks how a gambler can safeguard a wager and gain an advantage.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''ow' shows a dropped H, the Cockney habit; drop it likewise from HEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the edge over a rival means holding a slight superiority or upper hand in a contest.

clue.text: Battle before the match

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fight between armed forces
second meaning: the period of betrothal preceding a wedding, a match being a marriage

explanation.surface: A sporting contest is preceded by a fierce fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' suggests sport, but it is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a military clash and also a formal agreement to marry, the stage before the wedding.

clue.text: Dance music Nick Weaver finds the all-time low

parts.note: rock is popular music to dance to
Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A musician who plays dance tunes hits the lowest point of their career.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Bottom, the weaver who is given an ass's head, is one of the comic workmen in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the lowest possible level, as of prices or of someone's fortunes.

clue.text: Cricketer, artist and Aegean islander was Fisher, J

definitions.note: a noun phrase naming one example

parts.note: a bat is a batsman
RA, Royal Academician, is an artist
a Chian is a native of Chios, a Greek island in the Aegean

explanation.surface: A list of a sportsman, a painter and a Greek islander turns into a riddle about someone named Fisher.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Jeremy Fisher is the frog in Beatrix Potter's children's tale, written surname first like a register entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Batrachian refers to frogs and toads, and Beatrix Potter's angling Jeremy Fisher is a frog, so an example.

clue.text: Everything has gone wrong about this vessel

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go around the other piece
things gone wrong are out of order, so these letters must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
everything is all

explanation.surface: Disaster strikes aboard a ship where everything has gone awry.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large multi-decked sailing ship used by Spain for war and trade, so it is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: It's Cyril's eccentricity to be a song-writer

indicators.note: eccentricity is oddness of behaviour, so these letters are put into an odd order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cyril's oddball personality is what makes him a composer of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyricist writes the words of songs, so the term fits a song-writer, particularly one handling the lyrics.

clue.text: Cheese for which boy is about to compete in tournament …

indicators.note: the boy is about, or around, the other piece, so it encloses it

parts.note: a boy is a son
to tilt is to joust, the contest of a medieval tournament

explanation.surface: A lad is about to enter a contest whose prize is a cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'going to', but 'about' is the enclosing signal and 'to' starts the definition of TILT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilton is a strong blue-veined English cheese named after a village in Cambridgeshire where it was sold.

clue.text: Meritorious primate leads island rising

indicators.note: one who leads goes first, so the primate's name is placed in front

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury, Primate of All England

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means read upwards, so the island is spelt backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Italian island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A worthy ape heads an island that is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' suggests an ape, but it is a senior archbishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Laudable means deserving praise, which is the same as being meritorious or worthy of credit.

clue.text: More like one with heart of lion, it's said, or stone

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so we want a word with the same sound as the phrase before

parts.words: More like one with heart of lion
parts.note: someone lion-hearted is brave, so more like them is braver

explanation.surface: A comparison of courage with Richard the Lionheart, oddly ending in a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulder is a large rounded rock, so it is a very big stone.

clue.text: … while Émile chases frightful female for another

definitions.note: another cheese, following on from the previous clue

indicators.note: one who chases comes behind, so the novelist's name is placed after the other piece

parts.note: a Gorgon is a monstrous woman of Greek myth, such as Medusa, whose look turned people to stone
Émile Zola was the French novelist

explanation.surface: Continuing the tale, the French novelist pursues a terrifying woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue, so 'another' means another cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorgonzola is a blue-veined Italian cheese, so it follows Stilton as a second cheese in the linked pair of clues.

clue.text: Very unattractive fruit, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word spoken, so the fruit name stands for a word sounding the same

parts.note: the ugli is a wrinkled Jamaican citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a certain fruit looks hideous.
explanation.walkthrough: The ugli fruit, a tangerine-grapefruit cross, is spelt with a final I.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unpleasant to look at, the plain sense of being very unattractive.

clue.text: Such is one's descent by rope and a ladder initially

definitions.note: describes the descent, standing for the adjective

parts.note: a line is a rope, as on a ship
taken as written

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of the word before is kept

parts.note: the first letter of ladder

explanation.surface: A climber comes down by rope and a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descent' suggests climbing down, but it is ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineal descent passes in a direct line from parent to child, so the adjective describes one's ancestry.

clue.text: Heavenly fish!

parts.note: surface reading: an exclamation of delight at a delicious fish dish
setter's reading: belonging to the sky, as in the dappled cloud pattern named after this striped fish

explanation.walkthrough: A 'mackerel sky' is one covered in rippled cloud resembling the markings on the fish's back, so the fish is found in the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a sea fish, and its name is also given to a sky full of rows of small fleecy clouds.

clue.text: Disorderly flight of old party

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a defeated army's chaotic retreat
second meaning: an archaic word for a large fashionable evening gathering

explanation.surface: A long-established political group flees in confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old party' suggests a political party, but it means an 18th-century social assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a crushing defeat followed by chaotic retreat and, in older usage, a large evening reception.

clue.text: One with a wet chin making a run at Wembley

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who lets saliva trickle from the mouth

definitions.note: describes the person making the run
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a footballer taking the ball forward with small touches; Wembley is England's national football stadium

explanation.surface: A drooling figure charges forward at the famous London stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both letting spit run down the chin and running with a football kept close to the feet.

clue.text: Old German duchy providing capital for WI

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a former duchy in western Germany, ancestral home of the Dutch royal house
second meaning: the capital city of the Bahamas, in the West Indies

explanation.surface: A historic German territory supplies funds for some organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is the abbreviation for the West Indies; 'capital' looks like money but is a seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a historic German state and to the chief city of the Bahamas, which was named after the House of Orange-Nassau.

clue.text: Jack, model of industry, takes girl to a dance

indicators.note: taking someone along means having them follow, so the next piece is added at the end

parts.note: jack and tar are both old words for a sailor
the ant is the proverbial model of hard work
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A hard-working man called Jack escorts a girl to a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go to the ant, thou sluggard' (Proverbs) makes the ant the standard example of diligence.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarantella is a rapid whirling folk dance from southern Italy, so it is a kind of dance.
